BUILT ON OPEN DATA

Behind the numbers.

Public records, explicit assumptions and a reproducible pipeline.

Source & scope

New York City Taxi and Limousine Commission (TLC), Yellow Taxi Trip Records, January 2025. Zone names come from the official Taxi Zone Lookup Table.

These are taxi records, not Uber records, rental inventory or live vehicle locations. Counts measure recorded trips, not unmet demand, unique riders or fleet utilisation.

Official data portal ↗

Download original Parquet ↗

Taxi zone lookup CSV ↗

Quality & coverage

Keep January pickups, known borough zones, positive base fare, 1–180 minute durations, 0.1–100 mile distances and $1–$500 total amounts. Overlapping exclusions are counted once.

Exact duplicate rows are retained: no trip identifier exists to distinguish duplicate submissions from identical legitimate trips. Vendor accuracy and completeness are not guaranteed by TLC.

How route estimates work

Each directed pickup/drop-off pair needs at least 30 qualifying trips. The displayed fare is the median total_amount, including recorded taxes, tolls, surcharges and tips where captured. Cash tips are generally not recorded.

The fare range is the 25th–75th percentile of observed totals. It describes historical variation, not a prediction interval. Duration and distance are separate medians, not a single representative journey.

Unsupported routes show an empty state. No estimated values are invented.

Project boundaries

January 2025 is a reproducible snapshot, not a current operating feed. Trips reflect observed taxi activity and seasonality; the project makes no claim about causality or future demand.

Booking is a browser-only simulation. There is no matching engine, authentication, payments, driver network or backend booking database.
